MemelordAPIKeyCredential.x-credential-instructions: Create an API key in Memelord Developer Settings and paste it here. Generation and editing draw from your Memelord usage balance; account, discovery, and job-status reads are free.

MemelordEditMemeConfig.description: Change the text of an image meme you already generated. Pass the edit_handle from a generate_caption_meme / generate_ai_meme (or previous edit_meme) result together with a plain-language instruction; use the slot numbers from that result's caption_slots as target_index to change just one box. Re-renders the image and returns a fresh URL, the updated caption_slots, and a new edit_handle (earlier handles stay valid, so you can branch from any version). Handles only work for the account that created them. Billed against your usage balance.

edit_handle.title: Edit Handle

target_index.description: slot number (from caption_slots) of the one text box to change. Omit to let the editor decide.
target_index.title: Target Index

end_user_id.description: Optional opaque id of your end user behind this call (never an email or a name), for usage reporting. Same as the X-Memelord-End-User header.
end_user_id.title: End User Id

MemelordGenerateAiMemeConfig.description: AI-remixed image memes: Jester picks a meme template (or uses template_id), AI-edits the picture itself to fit the joke — swapping subjects, adding objects, or painting in people and products from reference_image_urls — then captions it. Use generate_caption_meme instead when you only want new text on an unchanged classic template. Returns signed image URLs plus template_id, caption_slots, and an edit_handle for edit_meme. Billed against your usage balance.

MemelordGenerateCaptionMemeConfig.description: Classic caption memes: Jester picks a real meme template from the library (or uses template_id), writes new text for its caption slots, and renders that text on the unchanged template image. The picture is never AI-edited or repainted — use generate_ai_meme for that. Returns signed image URLs plus template_id, caption_slots, and an edit_handle you can hand to edit_meme to change the wording. Use search_memes or get_trending_memes first if you want to pick the template yourself. Billed against your usage balance.

MemelordRunAgentConfig.description: Hand a natural-language request to Jester, Memelord's full meme agent — the same brain behind the Memelord chat. Jester decides what to do: search templates, caption a meme, remix a format, edit or generate an image, face-swap, make or caption a video, add text-to-speech or lipsync, convert to GIF, and more. Use this when a request does not map cleanly onto a specific tool ("turn this photo into a 3-panel meme about my cat", "make a video meme with the drake format about Mondays", "put my face on Elon"). Pass thread_id from a previous result to continue the conversation. Returns the assistant's message plus any images; videos come back as job_ids to poll with check_video_status. Billed against your usage balance.

MemelordRunGeminiOmniConfig.description: Run Gemini Omni, Google's Gemini video model, by name. Three lanes, picked from the inputs: EDIT an existing clip with a plain-language instruction (video_url, or video_job_id of a finished video on this account, plus prompt — "make it snow", "turn the car red", "add a top hat on the dog"); ANIMATE a still (image_url + prompt); or GENERATE a short clip from the prompt alone. Up to 3 reference_image_urls can ground identity, product, or style. Media must be public URLs the user provided — never invent or guess them; if the user gave you local files, upload them with upload_media first and pass the returned url. This runs Omni only: a safety-filter block comes back as an error instead of being re-routed to another model (for an edit that may try other engines use run_agent; for captioned meme clips use generate_video_meme; for other AI video models use run_video_model). Invalid requests come back as status "invalid_request" listing every problem, with nothing charged. Returns a job_id; poll check_video_status until completed (usually a couple of minutes). Billed against your usage balance once the render finishes.

MemelordRunGenjutsuConfig.description: Genjutsu character transpose: put a person or character into an existing video clip while keeping its motion, choreography, camera, timing, and audio ("put me in this music video", "swap the dancer for my character"). Needs the source clip (video_url, or video_job_id of a finished video on this account) and 1-8 photos in total of who to put in (character_image_urls for one person). Several people can be recast in ONE call: pass characters=[{target, image_urls}] with one entry per person, where target is who in the source clip they replace ("the king", "the guy playing chess") and image_urls are that person's own photos; all entries share the 8-photo cap. Both must be real media the user provided — never invent, guess, or substitute URLs. When the user gives you local photos or a local clip, upload each with upload_media first (clips over 3 MB via create_media_upload_url) and pass the returned urls. If anything is missing the call returns status "needs_input" listing everything still needed, with nothing started or charged: ask the user once, then call again. To generate new footage use run_video_model; for meme-template video clips use generate_video_meme. The clip's full cost is reserved from your usage balance before it starts; a balance that cannot cover it gets the usual usage-balance error and nothing is started or charged. Returns a job_id; poll check_video_status until completed. Billed against your usage balance per second of the source clip once the job finishes; the reservation is released if it fails.

MemelordRunVideoModelConfig.description: Generate new AI video footage with one model from list_video_models: from a prompt alone, a start frame (image_url, optional end_image_url), or reference images / clips / audio. Use this for original footage ("a cinematic drone shot over Tokyo at night", "animate this photo"). For a meme template turned into a captioned video clip use generate_video_meme; for still images use run_image_tool or generate_ai_meme; to put a person into an existing clip use run_genjutsu. Media must be public URLs the user provided — never invent or guess them; if the user gave you local files, upload them with upload_media and pass the returned url. Invalid requests come back as status "invalid_request" listing every problem, with nothing charged. The request's full cost is reserved from your usage balance before it starts; a balance that cannot cover it gets the usual usage-balance error and nothing is started or charged. Returns a job_id; poll check_video_status until completed (usually a few minutes). Billed against your usage balance per generated second once the job finishes; the reservation is released if it fails.

MemelordSearchMemesConfig.description: Search Memelord's template library of memes, video clips, and stickers. Default method "semantic_context" matches what a meme MEANS or depicts (natural-language queries like "when the deploy works on the first try"). Use "fulltext" for exact names and proper nouns ("drake", "spongebob"), "fuzzy" for misspellings, "semantic_combined" when visual identity matters, or "semantic_media" with media_url to find templates that look like a given image. Results come best match first and include ids you can pass as template_id to generate_caption_meme / generate_ai_meme / generate_video_meme / get_meme_template. Paging: each response has has_more and next_offset; to get the next page, repeat the exact same call (same query, method, filters, limit, min_score) with offset set to next_offset, and stop when has_more is false (next_offset is null). Pass ids you already have in exclude_ids only when starting a fresh search, not while paging, or the pages shift. Free.
